title: Roman Chair Leg Raise
overview: The Roman Chair Leg Raise is an effective exercise primarily targeting the lower abdominal muscles, specifically the rectus abdominis.It also engages the hip flexors and works the obliques and lower back muscles as secondary stabilizers.This movement strengthens the muscles in the lower torso, making it beneficial for improving posture, supporting the spine, and enhancing athletic performance.The controlled motion of the leg raise helps develop both flexibility and strength in the lower body, particularly in the abdominal and hip regions.
instructions: Position yourself on the Roman chair with your back against the pad and your legs hanging straight down.
Grip the handles for support. This is the starting position.
Lift your legs toward the ceiling by squeezing your lower abs. Keep your legs straight as you raise them.
Stop when your legs are about parallel to the floor or higher if you can.
Slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position with control, avoiding letting them drop quickly. This is one rep.
Perform the desired number of reps, focusing on keeping your core engaged throughout the movement.
tips: Always keep your core tight throughout the movement to protect your lower back and maximize the workout.
Control both the raising and lowering phases of the exercise to fully engage your abs and avoid using momentum.
Focus on keeping your legs straight as you lift them to better target your lower abs.
Exhale as you lift your legs, and inhale as you lower them.
Start with a lower range of motion if necessary, and gradually increase as you get stronger.
